label: prose:intro-parity-classification-discrepancy
html:
Arc IV applies the algebraic, geometric, and Plancherel machinery of Arcs I–III to the physical particle and nuclear mass spectrum. A central obstacle in classical knot-theoretic mass models is mirror-parity blindness: the classical Murnaghan–Nakayama character at q = 1 depends only on cycle type and cannot distinguish a chiral braid \beta from its mirror image \bar\beta, leaving the neutron–proton mass difference and parity-odd nuclear splittings unexplained.

This section proves that the classical character table is parity-blind, demonstrates how the q-deformed Hecke character at q \neq 1 closes the parity gap through its bar-odd (\sinh) component, and proves the universal Frobenius codimension theorem bounding the substrate action cost. Combining the parity-sensitive trace with the content-scaling correspondence yields the unified knot mass formula across the atomic atlas, whose terms organise the graded expansion of the categorical density \rho_K of the Gröbner–Shirshov mass identity.
